title: pcw-grapplearium-1996-world-heavyweight
label: Christian Kingsworth

won.source: Crowned in a 32-man Bunkhouse Brawl at Birthday Brawl; the show's own surviving text is truncated before naming the winner, but the promotion's own later broadcast and a rival federation's contemporaneous interview both bill him as the champion crowned that night.

lost.source: A rival federation's own March 1997 interview, quoting a wrestler explaining that Kingsworth "vacated the title" rather than defend it.

note: The vacancy is recorded from a rival federation's own words, not a document of this promotion's own.

title: pcw-grapplearium-1996-world-heavyweight
label: Gunnar "The Grizzly" Gaines

won.source: Awarded the vacated title; the same rival federation's interview that records Kingsworth's vacancy names Gaines as its recipient.

note: Retained and unified the title in a Texas Death Match against Steve Sampson at the Grapplearium, 11 April 1997 (35 minutes). The record does not preserve how the title passed from Gaines to the three contenders at Spring Showdown five weeks later.

won.source: Pinned Captain Midnight with the Hardcore Cutter at Spring Showdown, in a three-way match that had already been restarted once when Midnight refused an earlier disqualification win.

lost.source: Grade: user-attested. The community's own year-end poll credits this wrestler with three different federations' World titles in 1997; the promotion's own MLWO-crossover storyline that summer has him defending the belt the same day he challenges for another promotion's own title, a match the record attributes to Jak Martin.

title: pcw-grapplearium-1996-world-heavyweight
label: Jak Martin

won.source: Grade: user-attested, per the community's own corroboration of the same-day double title defense discussed above.

note: No further title update survives before the promotion's own closure by November 1997.

title: pcw-grapplearium-1996-columbia-valley
label: The Extremist

won.source: Billed as champion on the promotion's own April 1997 broadcasts, defeating Jack Kelly per the promotion's own account; the specific title-change match is not preserved in the documents read for this record.

note: Retained by No Contest against "American Nightmare" Gary Grayson at Spring Showdown (18 May 1997) after Thorn led Grayson to the ring already carrying the physical belt.

title: pcw-grapplearium-1996-columbia-valley
label: Drago

won.source: Already champion by the promotion's own account at New Year's Bash, "since defeating Mr. Deadly a few months back"; the title win itself predates the documents read for this record.

lost.source: The Extremist is billed as champion by the promotion's own April 1997 broadcasts; the record does not preserve the specific match in which the title changed hands.

note: Retained against The Prophet at New Year's Bash (2 January 1997, 34:13) and against Thorn at Birthday Brawl (28 January 1997, falls count anywhere, 29:59).

title: pcw-grapplearium-1996-television
label: "Hardcore" Matt Harris

won.source: Already champion by the promotion's own 28 January 1997 broadcast (Birthday Brawl); a rival federation's own broadcast the same week confirms the billing.

lost.source: "Maniac" Joe Colosi is billed as champion by Spring Showdown; the specific title-change match is not preserved in the documents read for this record.

note: A T'n'T challenge for the title on the same card is destroyed by capture truncation before its finish; the physical belt is separately billed as smashed by a rival federation's own talent around this time, with Harris still recognized as champion afterward.

title: pcw-grapplearium-1996-television
label: Thorn

won.source: Already champion by the promotion's own 10 November 1996 broadcast; the title win itself predates the documents read for this record.

lost.source: "Hardcore" Matt Harris is billed as champion by the promotion's own 28 January 1997 broadcast; the specific title-change match is not preserved in the documents read for this record.

note: Retained against "Master Of Pain" Barry Hart at the Grapplearium, 10 November 1996 (bridging back suplex).

title: pcw-grapplearium-1996-television
label: "Maniac" Joe Colosi

won.source: Already champion by the promotion's own 18 May 1997 broadcast; the title win itself predates the documents read for this record.

note: Retained against Dimension at Spring Showdown, 18 May 1997 (11:07).

title: pcw-grapplearium-1996-tag-team
label: Crusher Tech

won.source: Billed as champions early in 1997 by the promotion's own record; the specific title-change match is not preserved in the documents read for this record.

lost.source: Bigger Than Hollywood are billed as champions by the promotion's own April 1997 broadcast; the specific title-change match is not preserved in the documents read for this record.

note: Announced as the reigning PCW, EWA and CHAOS!!! tag champions simultaneously by New Year's Bash (2 January 1997), where they are shown preparing to defend against ASSpocalypse '97.

won.source: Billed as the new champions on the promotion's own Birthday Brawl broadcast, in commentary during the World Heavyweight Bunkhouse Brawl on the same card; the specific tag match and its opponents are not preserved in the documents read for this record.

lost.source: Crusher Tech are billed as new champions early in 1997, per the promotion's own record; the specific title-change match is not preserved in the documents read for this record.

title: pcw-grapplearium-1996-tag-team
label: Bigger Than Hollywood

won.source: Already champions by the promotion's own 11 April 1997 broadcast; the specific title-change match is not preserved in the documents read for this record.

lost.source: Crusher Tech regained the unified title in a caged elimination match at Spring Showdown, 18 May 1997 (45:13); the promotion's own record does not preserve when Bigger Than Hollywood first lost it between the unification and that match.

note: Unified the title with DPW's own Tag Team Championship at the Grapplearium, 11 April 1997, defeating DPW's own champions Negaforce.

won.source: Won a caged elimination match against Bigger Than Hollywood at Spring Showdown, 18 May 1997 (45:13).

title: pcw-grapplearium-1996-tag-team
label: Devil's Disciples

won.source: Already champions by the promotion's own 10 November 1996 broadcast; the title win itself predates the documents read for this record.

lost.source: The Rednecks are billed as new champions by the promotion's own broadcast the night of Birthday Brawl (28 January 1997); the specific title-change match is not preserved in the documents read for this record.

note: Retained against Crusher Tech at the Grapplearium, 10 November 1996 (Chop Shop Drop).
